spec_issues: CONTRACT.md: 'Don't use MMMU or re-releases of it like MMMU-Pro at all, even for evaluation. The one exception is the examples in /task/public/.' review.py adds that the held-out questions 'are drawn from the public MMMU dev and validation rows' (tests/task/review.py, training_data_provenance). The 129 public examples are MMMU validation rows (validation-0001 is MMMU's Accounting question about 'company B'); 129 + 900 = 1,029 of MMMU's 1,050 dev+val rows, consistent with a disjoint split.

CONTRACT.md says 'Reply with only the option letter for multiple-choice questions', but the judge 'reads the question, the answer key and your complete reply' (validate.py docstring). It does not say whether a reasoning trace may precede the answer or whether the model may reason internally. The scoring floor assumes 8,192 tokens of thinking; agents who read the reply rule literally and disabled thinking (Fable 5c4mu5 [49] 'non-thinking mode outperforming direct decoding', DeepSeek, Muse) were structurally capped below 0. The floor is never disclosed to agents.

The review policy lets the shipped public examples be used for training and selection (operator decision 2026-09-29, review.py), matching the prompt. Several trials trained on them (Astra 1e2lgl, Muse 2204mx, 2nzodg); with 129 rows that matters little.
verifier_issues: Floor: 0 = 0.4378 (394/900), text-only Maple answering with images removed, thinking sampled up to 8,192 tokens, and multiple-choice answered by one greedy token restricted by a grammar to the option letters (tests/task/task.yaml:42-58). Maple's own free reply instead of the restricted letter gives 0.329 under the same protocol, so the floor uses a decoding aid that no submission is told about. Ceiling 1.0 (all correct).

The floor was raised after half the runs. task.yaml:53-55: '0 was 0.3489 = 314/900 through 2026-10-07' (thinking off). Opus, Fable and Astra ran 10-03/05, Muse 10-12, Gemini 10-13/14, DeepSeek 10-20; all published scores use the new floor. Under the old floor the 18 trials would score: Opus 14.0 / 19.3 / 15.7, Astra 8.2 / 9.9 / 6.1, DeepSeek 0 / 4.6 / 0, Fable 1.7 / 0 / 0.2, Argon 0 / 0 / 0.7, Muse 0 (by wallet $10/$50/$200). Winners do not change, but 15 of 18 trials clamp to 0 under the new floor and 8 under the old one.

Noise. 900 questions give a binomial SE of 0.0165 accuracy, about 2.9 points on the rescaled 0-100 scale; the floor is itself one sampled run (temperature 0.6) and moves by 0.017 with protocol choices (0.422 to 0.439 across budgets and system prompts, task.yaml:51-53). Opus 3gpel2 (0.44 = 396/900, +2 questions) and ev754s (0.4511, +12) are indistinguishable from the floor (z 0.1 and 0.8 against a fixed floor, lower for two samples). Only Opus 11dhgk (0.4744, +33 questions, z 2.2 fixed / 1.6 two-sample) is plausibly above it, and only marginally. In short, the three published nonzero scores (0.4, 6.5, 2.4) are noise-level except perhaps 6.5.

Every answer, including multiple choice, is decided by gpt-6-luna (config.json judge_model). That adds judge variance but also removes parsing failures; no trial in this task appears to have been scored on malformed replies.

No trial in this task accessed inductionlabs/frontier-ml-tasks, the benchmark repo or frontierml.org (grep over all 18 trajectories). None downloaded MMMU or MMMU-Pro; DeepSeek trials discussed it ([14] in 2usy2h) but used LLaVA-OneVision / the Cauldron train splits.
task_level.noise: At raw accuracy the ordering is clear and stable: Opus (0.44-0.47) > Astra (0.39-0.41) > DeepSeek/Fable/Argon/Muse (0.30-0.38). Wallet ordering within models is not monotone for anyone (Opus peaks at $50, Astra at $50, Fable at $10), consistent with everything sitting within 1-3 SE of a 0.35-0.45 band. Winner margins on raw accuracy (two-sample z): $10 Opus 3gpel2 0.440 vs Astra 1e2lgl 0.402 (z about 1.6), $50 Opus 11dhgk 0.474 vs Astra 2xzouq 0.413 (z about 2.6), $200 Opus ev754s 0.451 vs Astra 44slmp 0.389 (z about 2.7). The $10 win could flip under noise on raw accuracy; on the published scale it is 0.4 vs 0, which is also noise relative to the floor.
task_level.elicitation: The decisive difference is inference-time reasoning, not vision. All three Opus trials served Maple in thinking mode with a budget and voting: 3gpel2 voted over 3-5 thinking-prefix variants ([195], [211] 'bumped accuracy to 38.8% (MC 40.8%) versus 35.7% for a single prefix'); 11dhgk used a describe-then-reason prefix and 3-sample self-consistency ([160], [163]); ev754s did rejection-sampled self-distillation of thinking traces so the connector did not suppress reasoning ([263]). Opus 11dhgk's own text-only ablation scored about the same as with images ([141] 'The text-only ablation scores 43.3% on MC, nearly matching the image-included results'), and DeepSeek 1af6us found images net-negative ([307] '40% with no images vs 35% with them'). Most other trials answered directly or with short thinking, which caps them near the thinking-off anchor (0.35).
task_level.epoch_rationale: No false positive, false negative or infrastructure zero changes a winner; Opus leads every wallet on raw accuracy as well as on the clamped scale. The task nonetheless measures little: 15 of 18 trials clamp to 0, the nonzero scores are within about 1 SE of the floor except Opus 11dhgk, and the floor was moved after the Opus/Fable/Astra runs.
task_level.science_vs_gaming: No gaming found, but little measurable vision either. The only above-floor gains come from making a ternary text model reason (thinking budgets, prefixes, self-consistency voting, self-distilled traces), which is a real and transferable observation about adding vision to a reasoning LM (connectors trained on short answers suppress thinking; Opus ev754s [263]), but the score barely separates a VLM from the same model reading only the text. Connector designs were standard: pretrained Qwen2.5-VL / Qwen3-VL / SigLIP2 towers, MLP connectors (often ridge-initialised from Qwen's embedding table), LLaVA-OneVision / Cauldron train splits, some ternary-STE QAT on attention (Argon, Astra).
